gaps.sentence: 'The shop closes at six,' she reminded me. She reminded me that the shop ___ at six.
gaps.explanation: Even habitual present simple backshifts after a past reporting verb: closes → closed.

gaps.sentence: "Congratulations!" — She ___ me on passing the exam.
'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
gaps.explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll carry those bags for you,' he said. He ___ to carry my bags.
gaps.explanation: Offers of help are reported as offered to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
gaps.explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw the accident happen,' the witness stated. The witness stated that he ___ the accident happen.
gaps.explanation: Past simple backshifts to past perfect after a past reporting verb: saw → had seen.

gaps.sentence: The witness ___ the police that he knew nothing.
gaps.explanation: Tell somebody that... — the personal object 'the police' requires told, not said.

gaps.sentence: 'I don't like seafood,' he confessed. He confessed that he ___ like seafood.
gaps.explanation: Present simple negative backshifts: don't like → didn't like.
